solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Heavy drinker from Madeira, say

definitions.meaning: someone who soaks up alcohol the way a soft porous thing soaks up water
Madeira cake is an example of a light baked cake of that kind

explanation.definitionFit: A boozer is informally called this absorbent thing, and a Madeira is a classic plain cake of this type.

clue.text: Dish produced by American company absorbed by another being switched

indicators.note: absorbed by says the first pair of pieces sits inside the switched second copy
the two halves of the second copy change places, so its front part goes to the back

parts.note: another American company, a second copy of US plus CO

explanation.surface: A corporate story: one American firm taken over by another in a business switch-around, producing something.
explanation.walkthrough: The second US CO, 'being switched', becomes CO US; 'absorbed by' puts the first US CO into its middle, CO(USCO)US.
explanation.definitionFit: This North African steamed semolina preparation is served as a dish in its own right.

clue.text: Stationery articles found in tabloid magazines?

parts.note: a tabloid is a popular newspaper, a paper
a magazine of a gun is also called a clip

explanation.surface: Office supplies apparently turning up inside the pages of popular glossy periodicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magazines' reads as reading matter but means ammunition holders, which are clips.
explanation.definitionFit: These small bent-wire fasteners for holding sheets together are standard stationery items.

clue.text: Quick break before this

definitions.meaning: put the word break in front and you get the morning meal, breakfast

explanation.definitionFit: Fast means quick, and break placed before it gives breakfast, the meal that breaks the overnight abstinence.

clue.text: Condemning two more names in experimental genetics

indicators.note: experimental suggests the letters are tried out in a new arrangement

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name, so two of them give two Ns

explanation.surface: A lab report: two extra names are added to research in experimental genetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' only places the two Ns among the letters of GENETICS before 'experimental' rearranges the whole pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentencing a convict is passing judgement on them, which is condemning them to a punishment.

clue.text: Unconvincing match needing hotel for women

indicators.note: needing one thing for another means a swap, here the letter for hotel takes the place of the one for women
needing one thing for another means a swap, here the letter for hotel takes the place of the one for women

parts.note: a twin is a match, an exact counterpart
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dating disappointment: a weak pairing needs a hotel for the women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needing' and 'for' together signal the swap of W out of TWIN for H.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin excuse is a weak one, flimsy and unconvincing to anyone hearing it.

clue.text: Manage to support most of finance for such an event

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes second
most of says the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a fund is money for something, finance
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: Organise something to back up most of the money raised at a charity gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer RUN under FUN 'supports' it; FUN comes from FUND with its last letter cut off. The clue reads as a whole: such events raise funds.
explanation.definitionFit: A fun run is a charity jogging race, exactly the sort of event the surface describes raising money.

clue.text: Put one's foot down, before start of evening rush

parts.note: to stamp is to bring one's foot down hard, here in the past tense

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone firmly asserts themselves before the evening rush begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put one's foot down' looks like insisting, but it is literally stamping, in the past tense STAMPED.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden headlong rush of a crowd or herd.

clue.text: A wicket, coming after support spread

indicators.note: coming after says the A and wicket pieces follow the support piece

parts.note: a prop is a support
a wicket is a small gate

explanation.surface: Cricket commentary: a wicket falls following some steady support play, then spreads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicket' suggests cricket, but here it is a small gate or door.
explanation.definitionFit: To propagate an idea or a plant is to spread or multiply it.

clue.text: Run down outside a place regularly visited

indicators.note: outside says the hunt piece goes round the letter A

parts.note: to run down quarry is to hunt it

explanation.surface: Someone jogs down past the outside of a favourite spot they keep visiting.
explanation.definitionFit: A haunt is a place one frequents, a favourite spot visited again and again.

clue.text: Emerging nation's final climb

indicators.note: the final of a word is its last letter

parts.note: an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: A rising country makes its last push upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nation's final' is the last letter of NATION; the apostrophe-s adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nascent is just coming into being, newly emerging and developing.

clue.text: Worker short on time has a fit

indicators.note: on says the worker and short pieces come after the time piece

parts.note: an ant is the crossword's standard worker
a short is a small measure of spirits, such as rum

explanation.surface: An employee whose break was cut short loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like an adjective about time, but it is a drink: a short is a nip of spirits such as RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is an outburst of bad temper, a fit of rage.

clue.text: I say nothing

parts.note: say signals an example, abbreviated e.g.
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone declares they will keep silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker, but it is the definition: the self.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychology the self, the 'I' of a person, is called by this Latin word for I.

clue.text: Summit cost must incorporate new heir

parts.note: the crown of a hill is its top, its summit

indicators.note: incorporate means take in, so the cost piece holds the new piece

parts.note: price means cost

explanation.surface: A business line: the peak cost needs to include a new successor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summit' looks like a meeting of leaders, but it is the top of a hill; 'must incorporate' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The heir apparent to a throne is the monarch's eldest son, styled this in many monarchies.

clue.text: Best actor is trained without a medical speciality

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters are drilled into a new shape
without says the letter A is left out of the letters being rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Theatre gossip: the top actor is untrained in a branch of medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange BEST ACTOR IS with the A taken away ('without a'); 'trained' is the rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstetrics is the branch of medicine dealing with pregnancy and childbirth.

clue.text: More or less a session after golf

indicators.note: after says the a and session pieces follow the golf piece

parts.note: a round is a complete game of golf
a bout is a session or spell of activity

explanation.surface: Roughly speaking, a meeting held once the golf is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golf' looks like the NATO letter G, but here a game of golf is a ROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundabout can mean approximately, in round figures, which is more or less.

clue.text: Dish from South Anerica — hot one

parts.note: US stands for America, here misspelt in the clue
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A menu entry: a spicy single dish from South America.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Latin American food, but the answer is Japanese, built from abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is the Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish or other toppings.

clue.text: Competition that might see people under fire?

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece placed under another comes second

parts.note: to fire someone is to sack them
a race is a people, a group sharing descent

explanation.surface: A contest in which some of the entrants risk being shot at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under fire' reads as being shot at; in a down entry it places RACE below SACK. The question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sack race is a children's sports-day contest in which runners hop along inside sacks.

clue.text: Short fleece for a runner in winter

indicators.note: short means a word with its last letter cut off

parts.note: a fleece is a sheep's skin

explanation.surface: A brief woolly jacket for someone jogging in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A runner in winter' suggests a jogger, but it is a runner on snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is a long narrow runner fixed to a boot for gliding over snow.

clue.text: Make one from backing asset in university

indicators.note: backing says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A college merger draws on an asset the university holds.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft named no hiding indicator: 'from' signals the extraction from 'asset in university', and 'backing' turns the run round.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite things is to join them together so that they become a single whole.

clue.text: A minion's disturbed by such a condition

indicators.note: disturbed suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, including the letter S

explanation.surface: A lackey troubled by sleeplessness.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'minion's' counts as a letter here; with A it gives eight letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is the condition of being unable to sleep, and it is what keeps a disturbed person awake.

clue.text: Urged by angry student with a relaxed attitude

indicators.note: by means beside, so the urged piece sits next to the others

parts.note: cross means angry
L is a learner, the crossword student
egged on means urged

explanation.surface: An irate student pushes someone into adopting a casual attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: L is a learner driver's plate, standard for a student.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting with legs crossed is a relaxed, informal posture, hence a laid-back attitude.

clue.text: Wild parties that show there's good in Conservatives sacking leader

indicators.note: in says the good piece goes inside the other
sacking the leader removes the first letter

parts.note: Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Proof of decent behaviour among the Tories, after they ditch their head, at their rowdy events.
explanation.walkthrough: TORIES are Britain's Conservatives; 'sacking leader' leaves ORIES, and 'in' puts G within.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgies are wild, unrestrained parties, typically of drink and sex.

clue.text: Collection box?

definitions.meaning: a collection of matching things, such as a group of stamps
box is slang for a television receiver

explanation.definitionFit: A set is a collection of items, and a TV set is colloquially the box.

clue.text: Number on a case of next occupier

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside letters

explanation.surface: Figures on a file belonging to the person who lives next door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case of next' is the outer pair of NEXT, giving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant is someone who occupies a property rented from a landlord.

clue.text: Send back something that might shoot a Republican soldier

indicators.note: send back says the pistol piece is turned round

parts.note: a Luger is a German pistol

explanation.surface: An order to return a gun that might be used against a Republican fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something that might shoot' is a Luger, a German pistol; 'Send back' signals the reversal, and a Republican soldier is a red herring for the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular is a professional soldier in a standing army, as opposed to a reservist.

clue.text: Fat boy grabbing last of sugar

indicators.note: grabbing says the boy piece holds another inside it

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An overweight child helping themselves to the remains of the sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard is rendered pig fat used in cooking.

clue.text: White gold plating pound pieces

indicators.note: plating says the gold piece covers the pound piece

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
LB is the abbreviation for a pound weight
chessmen are pieces, so pieces are men

explanation.surface: White gold coating some pound coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White gold' reads as one metal, but 'White' is the definition and gold is AU.
explanation.definitionFit: Albumen is the white of an egg.

clue.text: Condition regularly found in balconies

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A complaint that keeps cropping up on apartment balconies.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of BALCONIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition of inflamed spots.

clue.text: Profit from area covered by docking office worker

indicators.note: covered by says the area piece sits inside the other
docking an animal's tail cuts off its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a clerk is an office worker

explanation.surface: Earnings from a district looked after by a clerk who is having pay docked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Docking' cuts the K from CLERK; 'covered by' puts A inside CLER.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear a sum is to make it as net profit after expenses.

clue.text: Chaos caused by argument against merger

parts.note: the cons in pros and cons are arguments against
a fusion is a merger or joining together

explanation.surface: Disorder resulting from opposition to a corporate merger.
explanation.definitionFit: Confusion is a state of disorder and bewilderment, chaos.
